text:
sara (support): heads-up: Acme reported ~30% of requests to /v1/generate returned 503s over the last hour. They also saw a billing spike due to automatic retries. customer says it started after a large batch of long-context prompts.
ryan (oncall): ACK. seeing elevated 5xx rate for hosted-prod in datacenter us-west-2. alerting pager, collecting traces. any recent deploys? :eyes:
deploy-bot: rollouts: service/hosted-infer-controller had a canary deploy 2023-09-18T21:03Z -> image: redwood/infer:quant-v2. roll forward id=canary-42
lee (ml-infra): quick read on runner logs shows repeated "CUDA out of memory" followed by segfaults on pod infer-runner-7f9b. stack snippet: "cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (0x700)" then SIGSEGV.
josh (sre): copying logs. major pattern: OOM happens when context_len > 16384 combined with batch-size 8 and use_kv_prefetch=true. Also see contiguous evictions then container restart loop.
sara (support): customer repro steps: they replayed a synthetic load hitting: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood/quant-v2","batch_size":8,"prompts":[...long prompt ~20k tokens...]}' — they say failures reproducible.
lee (ml-infra): thanks. hypothesis: quant-v2 memory layout + kv-prefetch + batch aggregation triggers a transient overcommit on our GPU pools. new quantization pin changed memory footprint.
ryan (oncall): mitigation steps I pushed: 1) roll traffic from quant-v2 -> quant-v1 variant (safe fallback) 2) temporarily disable kv-prefetch for hosted-prod (config flag) 3) autoscaler: +20% guard capacity for GPU pool. doing now.
deploy-bot: traffic-routing: moved 35% -> redwood/quant-v1 at 3310001402. config change kv_prefetch=false applied at 3310001420.
sara (support): told Acme we routed them away from quant-v2 and asked them to stop automatic retries for 10m. they confirmed lower error-rate but still seeing occasional 503s. billing spike persisted for 45m, invoiced requests include retries.
emma (billing): noted. open a GC billing correction? can we produce an events log showing retry storms due to 503s to support credit? need request IDs and time windows.
josh (sre): will generate a trace map. quick query: requests with status=503 and retry_count>0 between 3310001000-3310001600. I can attach list of request_ids in the support ticket.
lee (ml-infra): repro instructions for eng: run the following locally against a dedicated small cluster: ```bash
# reproduce OOM locally (dev cluster)
for i in {1..20}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://dev-hosted.redwood/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/quant-v2","batch_size":8,"prompts":["'$(head -c 20000 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9')'"
  ]}' &
done
wait
```
Note: use a GPU with 48GB to observe OOM quickly. Also run with `KV_PREFETCH=1` env to match production.
sara (support): customer asked if auth/billing tokens caused this — they verified tokens ok and client didn't see 401s. this is server-side.
emma (billing): please include estimated tokenized units per failed request in the credits calculation. retries doubled token counts.
ryan (oncall): root-cause theory: memory regression after quant-v2 rollout combined with high-context prompts + aggressive prefetching. next: schedule a rollback of quant-v2 from hosted until we have a memory-safety patch. also start a bisect on quantization changes.
lee (ml-infra): log note: created issue INF-7982 with heap dumps and coredump links, assigned to team infer-runtime. adding reproducer and perf profile.
sara (support): sending customer timeline and current mitigations. I'll request a formal support credit while eng triages.
josh (sre): follow-up checklist: - persist coredump and nvcrash logs - capture nvml metrics around OOM windows - disable autoscaling burst that filled ephemeral nodes - add a canary that socks traffic to quant-v2 with stricter context limits (<=8k tokens).
sara (support): customer replied "thanks — error rate down to ~2% after route change. please let us know when safe to switch back; they want a postmortem and credit." :thumbsup:
emma (billing): starting pro forma review for credits. will need request_id list + token counts + impacted window.
ryan (oncall): I'll keep the thread updated. tagging @lee @josh for triage. moving to incident channel for formal postmortem after INF-7982 investigation.
lee (ml-infra): one last note — we should add a runtime check to refuse configs where batch_size*context_tokens > X on quantized backends to avoid silent OOMs. filing follow-up INF-7983.
sara (support): thanks team. closing loop with Acme in 30m with next steps and ETA for rollback validation.
